counterfactual_missing_items: considerable orthostatic changes in blood pressure and heart rate
sustained symptomatic bradycardia or sinus pauses
acute pathologic changes on cranial CT
decisive_items: Sinus rhythm with right bundle-branch block
response.rationale: C1 precisely captures the ECG evolution from RBBB with left anterior fascicular block to RBBB with left posterior fascicular block, i.e. alternating fascicular block, which explains syncope as a high-risk cardiac conduction disturbance. R4 names the same category but lacks the discriminating subtype. R3 only supports hypertensive heart disease and does not explain the conduction abnormality or syncope; R1 is not supported because there are no sinus pauses, arrest, or marked symptomatic bradycardia; R5 is directly contradicted by stable vital signs without orthostatic changes.

rejected.why: Echocardiographic LVH supports hypertensive heart disease but does not explain the alternating fascicular block or syncope.
A single PAC and rate of 58 bpm do not meet sick sinus syndrome criteria; no sinus pauses or symptomatic bradycardia are present.
The history suggests presyncope, but the vital signs explicitly lack considerable orthostatic blood pressure or heart rate changes.
